earlier_scan.note: Glottolog entry retired/spurious: Welaung is a place name for Nga La (Matu Chin) [hlt]; no description of a distinct variety.

sources.citation: So-Hartmann, Helga. 2009. A Descriptive Grammar of Daai Chin. STEDT Monograph 7. Berkeley.
sources.note: Welaung appears only in Bradley's (1997) Southern Chin list (p. 23) and Grierson's (1904) classification figure (p. 24). The stress description in the book is of Daai [dao], not of Welaung/Rawngtu.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Chin, Rawngtu [weu]'. Dallas: SIL. (Internet Archive copy 2016-03-04)
sources.note: Nothing. Alt names Rongtu, Shimi, Welaung; 5,000 (2008); Mindat township (Chin State) + 2 villages in Htilin township (Magway); dialects Kyonnam, Welaung, Boishi, Shitwanu; lexical similarity 84-89% with Matupi Daai [dao], 71-83% with Matu [hlt]; 'Typology SOV; negation is marked after the verb.'

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (Ethnologue Editor, SIL). 2011. Change Request 2011-014: weu 'Welaung' -> 'Chin, Rawngtu' (adopted 2012-02-03).
sources.note: Nothing. Name change only: 'Welaung is the name of one village within a broader language group that calls itself Rawngtu Chin today.' Cites an unpublished 2008 Myanmar sociolinguistic survey of 7 Rawngtu villages incl. Welaung (wordlists, comprehension testing); no phonology.

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 1997. Tibeto-Burman languages and classification. In Bradley (ed.), Tibeto-Burman languages of the Himalayas (Papers in Southeast Asian Linguistics 14), 1-72. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Comparative classification that lists Welaung as a Southern Chin language (seen via So-Hartmann 2009: 23); classification only, but it is the modern secondary source that keeps the name alive and may cite its data source.
sources.venue: Tibeto-Burman languages of the Himalayas (Papers in Southeast Asian Linguistics 14)

sources.citation: Hartmann(-So), Helga. 1988. Notes on the Southern Chin languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 11(2): 98-119.
sources.note: No Welaung/Rawngtu hit in the scanned; p. 98: 'Tone and/or register was not marked consistently in most of the lists, so I have not attempted to discuss it.' No stress statement for any variety.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III: Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. pp. 329-330 'Southern Chin sub-group'.
sources.note: Nothing for Welaung. Only Rainey's ethnographic notes (Welaung Chins at the headwaters of the Myittha river) and 'We have very little information with regard to the dialects spoken by these tribes.' No specimen or vocabulary for Welaung; the tone remarks on p. 333 concern Khyang/Sho.
sources.venue: III Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III: Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups

sources.note: Nothing. Comment: 'Welaung is a place name belonging to the Nga La [hlt] (or Matu Chin) language, so the Welaung [weu] entry is spurious.' Cites Hartmann 1988: 98-99. Glottolog reference search for 'Rawngtu' and 'Welaung' returns no records.
